scientific_quality.justification: A real pseudo-spectral 3D kinematic ABC-dynamo generator, validated against exact identities, feeds a six-arm comparison of constraint routes (free, loss, curl-of-potential design, in-loop and post-hoc projection, coloured prior) at 16^3 with Rm=24 held out. The solver validation is the solid part. The learning study is far too small to carry the findings drawn from it: networks of base width 6 trained for 120 steps, 8 samples per group, one seed, AUC all NaN, ensemble spread far below the data. The team says so, but still words several findings as results ('in-loop projection beats post-hoc', 'the prior is a constraint mechanism'). The report was not cleaned: empty table placeholders, a duplicated summary item, sections and tables cited that do not exist, and a text claim (decay rate reproduced to 2.4e-6) contradicted by its own Table 1 and results/exp0_validation.json (relative error 2.8e-3, above the stated 1e-4 expectation). No dynamo threshold was bracketed (all three Rm decay) and this is stated.

fable.summary: Team A built and validated a 3D kinematic dynamo solver and compared six ways of enforcing the divergence-free constraint in conditional flow matching. The comparison ran at a very small scale after a lost GPU and three re-scopes, so only the exact-versus-soft divergence result is firm. The report is candid about its limits but was left unfinished, with placeholders and a few figures that do not match its own result files.

scientific_quality.justification: A compact and honest study on true 2D incompressible MHD (own pseudo-spectral solver, 3200 runs with random nu and eta), comparing six ways of enforcing the divergence-free constraint that cover the three routes of the subject: none, post-hoc and per-step Leray projection, loss penalty, stream-function/potential parameterisation, projection layer. Metrics include divergence, kinetic and magnetic spectra, Wasserstein distances of energy, dissipation, cross-helicity and mean-square potential, critical-point counts of A, and a parameter-response slope, each read against a data noise floor and on a held-out band of viscosity. All numbers are in results/metrics_raw.json and table.md and agree with the report. The report states its weakness at the top: one seed, 400 steps on a width-24 network on a shared CPU, so rankings are descriptive; it also records a bug that made the loss arm identical to the baseline, fixed before the reported run. Limits: no multi-seed, the solver check (energy conservation to 1e-6) has no log, the noise floor compares different parameter sets, topology detector admittedly crude, no engagement with the literature.

fable.summary: Team G compared six ways of making conditional flow matching divergence-free on 2D MHD fields produced by its own solver, with a noise floor and a held-out parameter band. Hard constraints and projections reach round-off divergence and the stream-function model gives the best spectra, on a single under-trained seed that the report flags from its first line. A framework failure took away the GPU and half an hour, which explains the small scale.

scientific_quality.justification: A well-organised pilot with good experimental habits: a Burgers benchmark and a 2D MHD solver with independent initial conditions per sample, an in-distribution grid and a never-seen interpolation grid, a PCA-truncation floor that separates representation error from model error, reference floors for the energy balance and PDE residual, up to three seeds, Wilcoxon tests, and a decision log that records a rejected dataset, a rejected model and an evaluation that had read the wrong checkpoints. The report says clearly that the physics loss does not improve the distributions and that the PDE-residual column is not informative. Three reservations. (1) The unconstrained baseline is trained in a different space (2312 coefficients, 256 fields, 1600 steps) and its training log shows no learning on validation (1.966 after training vs 1.970 at step 0), so 'divergence-free structure is consequential' compares a working latent model with an untrained one; exact zero divergence of the structural model is true by construction. (2) The headline benefit of the physics loss, the parameter-response slopes, comes from seed 0 only, is called 'almost exact', and the claim that the ranking holds on the interpolation grid is contradicted by the numbers given (b_Rm 0.111 for physics vs 0.132, data 0.179). (3) The generative models are weak (validation loss 1.52 against about 2.0 untrained, energies 27-32% off, spread 1.7 times the data, PDE residual 100 times the reference), in 2D, with an MLP on 32 PCA components. The result tables behind the report (results/metrics.json, metrics_table.md, sanity_checks.json) are in the repository listing but not in the extract given to the jury, so the tabulated values were checked against code and training logs only.

fable.summary: Team H ran a CPU-only pilot on Burgers and 2D MHD, comparing an unconstrained model, an exactly divergence-free one and a physics-informed loss, with truncation floors, unseen parameters and significance tests. Its sober reading, that the soft physics loss does not improve the distributions, is well argued; its two positive claims are weaker, because the unconstrained baseline did not train and the parameter-response gain rests on one seed. The study is well documented and reproducible, at 2D pilot scale.

scientific_quality.justification: Not delivered; no report, no run, no result file. The repository holds about 90 kB of package code (operators, metrics, backbones, generative models, ROM and data-assimilation modules) with no trace of execution. The '3D MHD dynamo dataset' is not a simulation: fields are hand-built from ABC modes and filtered noise, with a critical Rm of 22, polarity states and reversal excursions assigned by random draw and energies rescaled to prescribed laws; the 2D 'channel flow' is built the same way. Results on such data would say nothing about MHD, and the code comments present these constructions as physics. The plan (diffusion and flow matching, four constraint strategies, ROM and DA) was far beyond the means.

scientific_quality.justification: A clean, well-trained single-benchmark study: a pseudo-spectral 2D Kolmogorov-flow dataset at four measured Reynolds numbers, a 7 M-parameter conditional U-Net trained 3000 steps per variant on a GPU, four strategies (none, divergence penalty, stream-function design, Helmholtz projection) evaluated on 256 samples per Re, with all numbers in results/metrics.json. The orders-of-magnitude findings are solid (penalty lowers divergence by 26% only, design and projection reach 1e-6), the failure of the stream-function model is reported and its cause given as a conjecture, and a matched-versus-mismatched Re check shows that the conditioning carries information. Limits: one seed; no held-out Reynolds number (test fields are later snapshots of the same four runs); no noise floor; only 64 reference fields; two sentences on the energy of the projected model are more favourable than the JSON (ratio 0.855-0.955, not 0.92-0.96; up to 14.5% low, not 5-8%); and nothing beyond 2D hydrodynamics.

context.effect: No visible loss of scientific content; the Hub failure is not held against the team. Scaleway GPU quota at zero forced Runpod, at the cost of a few minutes.

fable.summary: Team F compared a divergence penalty, a stream-function design and a sampling-time projection for conditional flow matching on 2D Kolmogorov flow, with well-trained models and traceable metrics. Projection and design give exact divergence control, the penalty does not, and the stream-function model failed statistically, which the team reports. The work stops at the first stage of the subject: no magnetic field, no 3D, one seed.

scientific_quality.justification: The most rigorous study of the race. An analytic heat benchmark and a nonlinear 3D incompressible MHD solver (u and b, RK4, de-aliased) with operator tests and a temporal convergence check; baseline and soft-loss flow-matching models with three training seeds each; projection and energy-budget corrections at sampling; independent 128/256-trajectory test sets, seen and interpolated parameters; an independent reference-versus-reference floor on every metric; and a matched-noise intervention that tests the parameter response. Every number of the report is in results/summary.md and the corrected JSON files, and the team reads them soberly: the soft loss helps on heat and not on MHD, corrections are exact by construction, the parameter response is too weak, models remain 4-5 times above the floor. The limits are of scale and of scope: 8^3 with modes |k|<=2 is a very low-dimensional decaying system, the design route (potential parameterisation) is absent, loss weights are untuned, and the topology metric is a coarse proxy. Two thirds of the time allowance were left unused.
evidence: results/summary.md: heat interpolation residual 0.487 -> 0.266, energy W1 0.159 -> 0.098; MHD interpolation divergence 0.178 / 0.209 / 1.18e-7, budget 0.0090 / 0.0100 / 1.8e-8, reference floor rows
results/convergence.json: 1.86e-6, 1.12e-7, 6.47e-9 (fourth order)
results/operator_checks.txt: PASS projection, divergence, MHD energy identity, heat mode, budget correction
artifacts/: 12 checkpoints, data.pt, results_corrected.json, metrics.npz; code/mhd.py, evaluate_mhd.py, test_physics.py

compliance.justification: Simple PDE first, then 3D MHD with both fields, conditioning on (nu, eta) with held-out interpolation points, loss and sampling routes, all four metric families (helicity and topology as declared proxies), data and models published with cards, one-command reproduction with stored checkpoints. Missing: the model-design route, any downstream ROM/DA use, turbulent or dynamo regimes; the reference list is treated as not applicable and only one of the five subject references is cited. The compliance matrix under-claims rather than over-claims.

fable.summary: Team D delivered a small but carefully controlled comparison of soft-loss and sampling-time constraints on an analytic heat benchmark and a 3D periodic MHD system. Three seeds, independent test sets and reference floors back every claim, including the negative ones. The study is limited by its tiny grid and by stopping after twenty minutes with most of its means unused.

scientific_quality.justification: Not delivered, graded on the repository, which holds a complete and unusually candid report with result files that back it. Three benchmarks (exact Burgers, 2D and 3D kinematic induction), five strategies over the three routes, three seeds on Burgers with the single-seed ranking explicitly withdrawn, failures reported as failures (the 2D stream-function head does not train; no polarity reversal exists in the benchmark, so the axial-sign metric is declared empty). But the experiments are at toy scale even for the means: 9 training fields and 4 test fields in 2D, 16 and 4 in 3D at 8^3 over 0.03 time units, 200-300 Adam steps, trainings of 2 to 6 seconds. Most models do not work (relative L2 about 1.0 for all unconstrained MHD models, 0.42 on Burgers), so the comparison is between failed generators. The one positive MHD result (3D energy penalty, 1.00 -> 0.43) is one seed on four fields. The target is a single deterministic field per parameter value, scored by relative L2: this is conditional regression, not the generation of diverse fields. The <A^2> column of the 2D table does not match results/mhd2d/metrics.json for any of the five rows. The ABC-flow reference field has a relative divergence of 5.5e-3 in results/reference.json, not discussed.

fable.means: The mission spent 4.80 of 5 USD of model calls in 23 minutes, through contexts of about 200 thousand tokens per call, and stopped without delivering; no GPU was obtained. The experiments themselves cost seconds of CPU, so the science is far below what the time allowance permitted, and the budget was used poorly.

incidents_outside_control: First run not metered and set aside; restart from scratch at 00:40:36
At 00:59 the framework ended the mission on a worst-case cost rule since relaxed; resumed at 01:00 (partly outside)
Scaleway quota refusals on every type tried
context.effect: The restart gave a full allowance. The 00:59 stop cost about a minute; the exhaustion of the model budget by 01:03 is the team's own, and is what prevented delivery, a larger study and the publication. The absence of a GPU explains the CPU scale but not datasets of nine fields.

Toy scale: 9 to 16 training fields, 4 test fields, 200-300 steps; most generators fail

One table column not backed by its result file; DELIVERY.md and Hub publication cited but absent
fable.summary: Team I did not deliver: it used almost its whole model budget in 23 minutes. Its repository still holds an honest three-benchmark comparison of design, loss and sampling constraints, with negative results clearly reported. The experiments are too small for most models to learn, so only the Burgers conditioning and the sampling-time corrections stand as measured results.

scientific_quality.justification: The design was sound and of the right scale for a GPU (2D Kolmogorov flow with a held-out Re, a 3D solenoidal helical family with four strategies), but what was measured is thin: one 2D model, three sampling variants, three mean numbers, all negative, plus training losses for the 3D runs. The 3D evaluation, which is the comparative study, never finished. The 2D result is itself doubtful: re-projecting samples on the training spectrum makes the spectrum error worse (2.27 vs 1.31), and the probe energies of the data (0.84 at Re=62.5) do not match the training mean quoted in the text (3.11), which points to non-stationary data or an evaluation bug rather than to the conclusion drawn. The discussion nevertheless states conclusions on the 3D strategies that no evaluation backs. Several numbers are cited from results/meta2d.json, meta3d.json and metrics.json, which are not in the repository.

fable.summary: Team C planned a two-benchmark comparison of where to inject physics into conditional flow matching and trained its models on a rented GPU. Solver bugs and a session cut left only a small, negative 2D evaluation; the 3D comparison was trained but never evaluated. The report is honest about the cut but draws conclusions the delivered files do not support.
